evidence.quote: a sanctuary so revered that it forms one of the four sacred Char Dhams of Hindu pilgrimage

supporting over 150,000 fisher-

evidence.quote: The city's name is derived from "Tribhubaneswar," meaning "Lord of the Three Worlds,"

LIN1.claim: The 11th-century Lingaraj Temple, built by King Jajati Keshari, rises 180 feet; its 40-acre complex has 150 smaller shrines.

the imposing Lingaraj Temple towers 180 feet high

Closing time - 07:00 PM

KUC1.claim: The Khandagiri and Udayagiri caves are Jain rock-cut monasteries from the 2nd century BCE, under Emperor Kharavela; open 9 am to 9 pm.

evidence.quote: The Khandagiri and Udayagiri Caves date back to the 2nd century BCE, during the reign of Emperor Kharavela of the Kalinga dynasty.

Closing time - 09:00 PM

DHA1.claim: Dhauli, 8 km from Bhubaneswar, has a rock carrying Ashoka's edicts and a carved elephant marking his change of heart after the Kalinga war.

evidence.quote: Located 8 km from Bhubaneswar, the Dhauli Giri Hills have a mass of rock by the side of the road leading to its summit. Engraved on this mass of rock are major Edicts of Ashoka.
The mass of rock at the Hills also bears carvings of the head and forelegs of an elephant emerging from the rock

BHK1.claim: Bhitarkanika, 672 sq km in Kendrapada district, is India's second-largest mangrove ecosystem, with 215 bird species including eight kingfishers.

evidence.quote: Spanning over a vast area of 672 square kilometers
stands as the second-largest mangrove ecosystem in India
The sanctuary is home to 215 bird species, including eight varieties of kingfishers

BHK2.claim: The nearest airports are Bhubaneswar and Kolkata; boats leave from Chandbali. Open 6 am to 6 pm.

evidence.quote: The nearest airports are located in Bhubaneshwar and Kolkata, while waterways are accessible through Chandabali, Ragnagar, and Gupti.
Opening time - 06:00 AM
Closing time - 06:00 PM

AP1.claim: Andhra Pradesh, on the south-east coast, is India's seventh-largest state and the home of Kuchipudi dance.

evidence.quote: Andhra Pradesh is India's seventh-largest state and is situated along its southeastern coastline.
Known for its rich cultural history and traditional dance forms like Kuchipudi and Vilasini Natyam

AP2.claim: Andhra is famous for fiery Guntur chillies, and the Tirupati laddu has a Geographical Indication tag.

evidence.quote: boasting one of the hottest chili peppers worldwide - Guntur chili is considered among them.
Be sure to try the iconic Tirupati Laddu from Venkateswara Temple Tirumala; its sweet offering holds Geographical Indication status

AP3.claim: Talakona is the state's highest waterfall at 270 feet; Pulicat is a major lagoon for migratory birds.

evidence.quote: Talakona Waterfall stands as Andhra Pradesh's highest waterfall at an impressive height of 270 feet
Pulicat Lake - one of India's two-largest lagoons, known as an important habitat for migrating birds

TPT1.claim: Tirupati has been a centre of Vaishnavism since the 5th century; the Govindaraja Swamy Temple in town was completed in 1130 CE.

evidence.quote: Tirupati's history as a centre of Vaishnavism (devotion to Lord Vishnu and his avatars) dates back to the 5th century A.D.
the grandeur of the Govindaraja Swamy Temple, completed in 1130 CE

TML1.claim: The Sri Venkateswara Temple (Tirupati Balaji) on the Tirumala Hills, about 980 m high, draws around 24 million devotees a year and is run by the TTD.

evidence.quote: The Sri Venkateswara Swami Temple , also known as the Tirupati Balaji Temple, is the crowning jewel of Tirupati's spiritual legacy.
Tirumala Hills, which are part of Seshachalam Hills range, rise to approximately 980 metres (3,220 ft) above sea leve
attracts around 24 million devotees annually
The temple is administered by the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD)

TML2.claim: The Tirupati laddu is the temple's famous prasadam; at Vaikunta Ekadasi the 'gates of Vaikunta' are opened.

evidence.quote: One of the most sacred rituals performed at the Tirumala Temple is the offering of "Tirupati Laddu,"
even more fascinating is the annual Vaikunta Ekadasi festival, celebrated with great fervour at the Tirumala Temple!

SKH1.claim: The Srikalahasti Shiva temple on the Swarnamukhi river dates to the 5th century; its 120 m Rajagopuram was built by the Vijayanagara Empire.

evidence.quote: Settled on Swarnamukhi River’s bank
The origin of Srikalahasti Temple dates back to the 5th century when the inner temple was constructed.
In the 16th century, the empire constructed the majestic 120m high main gopuram.
Opening time - 05:30 AM
Closing time - 09:30 PM

VSK1.claim: Visakhapatnam, on the Bay of Bengal, has the INS Kursura submarine museum and the Bavikonda Buddhist site 15 km away; its airport is close to the centre.

evidence.quote: One of the most notable architectural monuments in Visakhapatnam is the Submarine Museum (INS Kursura).
Bavikonda Stupa, located on a hill about 15 km (9.3 mi) northeast of Visakhapatnam city
Visakhapatnam airport is located very close to the city centre

BOR1.claim: The Borra Caves, 88 km from Visakhapatnam in the Ananthagiri hills, are limestone caves at about 705 m, among the largest in India and up to 80 m deep.

evidence.quote: Situated 88 kilometres from Visakhapatnam, the Borra Caves grace the crown of Ananthagiri hills in Araku Valley.
These limestone caves, at an elevation of about 705 m, are the largest in India
Reaching depths of up to 80 m
Opening time - 10:00 AM
Closing time - 05:00 PM

ARK1.claim: Araku Valley is a hill station in the Eastern Ghats about 111 km from Visakhapatnam, known for coffee plantations.

evidence.quote: Araku Valley is a hill station in the Alluri Sitharama Raju district of Andhra Pradesh , India , located 111 km from Visakhapatnam .
the Andhra Pradesh Forest Department developed coffee plantations in the valley

ARK2.claim: Nearby are the Tyada railway tunnel, Damuku viewpoint and Ananthagiri coffee plantations.

evidence.quote: Cover intriguing attractions such as the Tyada Railway Tunnel, Damuku Viewpoint, Ananthagiri Coffee Plantation, Padmapuram Gardens, and the breathtaking Araku Valley.

AMR1.claim: Amaravati was a centre of Buddhist learning; its Mahachaitya stupa dates to the Mauryan era, and the site is open 8 am–6 pm, closed Fridays.

evidence.quote: It was also the centre of Buddhist learning and art, and Buddhist followers from many Southeast Asian countries visited.
The history of the Amaravati Mahachaitya dates back to the 3rd century during the Mauryan Empire and flourished during the Satavahana dynasty.
Opening time - 08:00 AM
(Closed on Fridays)

AMR2.claim: Kondapalli Fort is about 20 km away; Guntur's chilli yard, Asia's largest, about 40 km.

evidence.quote: The Kondapalli Fort is around 20 kilometres from Amaravati
The largest chilli market in Asia, called “Guntur Mirchi Yard”, is about 40 kilometres from Amaravati.

UND1.claim: The Undavalli caves, cut from sandstone beside the Krishna, hold a 5 m reclining Vishnu; open 9 am to 6 pm.

evidence.quote: Situated next to the beautiful Krishna River in Guntur, the Undavalli Caves
A deity, believed to be Lord Vishnu, rests in peaceful repose—a statue that spans an astonishing 5 meters.
Opening time - 09:00 AM
Closing time - 06:00 PM

TG1.claim: Telangana became India's newest state on 2 June 2014; its history runs through the Satavahanas, Kakatiyas, Qutb Shahis and Asaf Jahis.

evidence.quote: On June 2, 2014, Telangana was officially designated as the newest and youngest state within India.
with deep-rooted connections to significant empires such as the Satavahanas, Kakatiyas, Ikshvakus, Qutb Shahis, and Asif Jahis

TG2.claim: Hyderabad's food runs from dum biryani to qubani ka meetha and Irani chai.

evidence.quote: Dum Ka Biryani, Qubani Ka Meetha, special Hyderabadi biryani, Irani Chai, Sakinaalu, and Sarva Pindi are some of the delectable specialties.

TG3.claim: Nirmal paintings and wooden toys have been made since the 14th century.

evidence.quote: Nirmal painting and Nirmal toys have been cherished throughout India since the 14th century

HYD1.claim: Hyderabad, the old capital of the Nizams and the 'City of Pearls', is known for the Laad Bazaar of bangles near Charminar and Hussain Sagar lake, dug in 1562.

evidence.quote: Hyderabad became the capital of the Nizams
Also known as the ‘City of Pearls’
The beautiful bustling bazaar near Charminar is an extremely popular and thriving market known as Laad Bazaar or Choodi (Bangles) Bazaar.
it was excavated in 1562 AD during the reign of Ibrahim kuli Qutub Shah

CHM1.claim: The Charminar's four minarets rise 48.7 m; entry closes at 5 pm, and it is lit up from 7 to 9 pm.

evidence.quote: It features a four-sided archway and towering minarets that reach 48.7 meters above ground level.
Closed for entry after 05:00 PM.
(The monument looks mesmerising when illuminated from 07:00 PM to 09:00 PM)

GOL1.claim: Golconda Fort, 9 km from Hussain Sagar, dates back to 1143 and passed from the Bahmanis to the Qutb Shahis; a light and sound show runs in the evening.

evidence.quote: only 9 km from Hussain Sagar Lake. It dates back to 1143
A Light and Sound show is held in the evenings where the glorious past of Golconda Fort is narrated
Opening time - 09:00 AM
Closing time - 05:00 PM

SJM1.claim: The Salar Jung Museum, opened by Nehru in 1951 and an Institution of National Importance since 1961, holds Aurangzeb's sword and Tipu Sultan's wardrobe; open 10 am–5 pm.

evidence.quote: The magnificent Salar Jung Museum was inaugurated by the Prime Minister of India, Jawahar Lal Nehru in 1951.
In 1961, through an ‘Act of Parliament’ the Salar Jung museum along with its library was declared an ‘Institution of National Importance’.
Aurangzeb's sword, daggers that belonged to Shah Jahan and Jehangir, and the wardrobe of Tipu Sultan
Opening time - 10:00 AM

WGL1.claim: Warangal, about 150 km from Hyderabad, was the seat of the Kakatiyas; its Kakatiya Kala Thoranam gateway appears on Telangana's emblem.

evidence.quote: It is about 150 km  from Hyderabad.
Once the seat of the Kakatiya dynasty
It is a symbol of Warangal's rich history and cultural heritage and is depicted on the emblem of Telangana state.

WGL2.claim: The Bathukamma flower festival is celebrated during Navaratri.

evidence.quote: The lively Bathukamma festival, observed during Navaratri

RAM1.claim: The Ramappa (Rudreshwara) Temple at Palampet, built in 1213, about 200 km from Hyderabad, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (2021) famed for its 'floating bricks'.

evidence.quote: officially known as the Ramappa Temple, built in 1213 CE
around 200 km northeast of Hyderabad in Telangana
This tower is made of lightweight porous bricks known as ‘floating bricks’
Designated 2021 (44th session )

RAM2.claim: Open 6 am to 6 pm; Ramappa Lake is less than 1 km away.

evidence.quote: Opening time - 06:00 AM
Closing time - 06:00 PM
Less than 1 km away lies the serene Ramappa Lake

TPL1.claim: Built in 1163 by the Kakatiya king Rudra Deva at the foot of Hanamkonda hill, the star-shaped temple honours Shiva, Vishnu and Surya; open 5 am–9 pm.

evidence.quote: built in 1163 AD by Kakatiya ruler Rudra Deva
Erected at the foot of the Hanamkonda Hill
where three deities are worshipped - Lord Shiva, Lord Vishnu and Surya
Opening time - 05:00 AM

WGF1.claim: Warangal Fort, of the Kakatiyas who ruled 1175–1324, has three concentric walls; a 50-minute sound and light show runs at dusk. Open 10 am–7 pm.

evidence.quote: who reigned over the Deccan Plateau from 1175 to 1324 CE
Warangal Fort is protected by three concentric circular walls
For 50 minutes, the fort becomes a can
Opening time - 10:00 AM

LAK1.claim: Laknavaram Lake, about 70 km from Warangal, was built by the Kakatiyas from three valleys and is ringed by forest.

evidence.quote: situated near the Laknavaram village around 70 kilometres from Warangal
This magnificent body of water emerged from the union of three narrow valleys
The origin of the lake dates back to the rule of the Kakatiyas.
